note: Every place in prose that states how many rules the checker has. rules.json is the source of truth; these are the copies. They drifted to 24 while rules.json carried 31 and nothing noticed for over a week -- see AGENTS.md, gate A9. A pin that matches NOTHING is a failure, not a pass: a detector that reads nothing and a repository with nothing wrong produce the same green tick.

sweep.why: The pins only find what someone remembered to pin. The sweep is the net for a NEW count that appears in prose without being registered here. It was calibrated against the real corpus: two or three digit numbers within 40 characters of rule/check/checker/catalogue, in markdown only.

pins.pattern: reports faults before you open it: (\d+) of them
pins.why: The 'What is included' table. Escapes a naive grep for 'N rules' entirely -- the noun is nine words away -- which is exactly why it is pinned by sentence rather than found by pattern.
The 'About the checker' section named in AGENTS.md as one of the three sites that must be updated when the count moves.

The worked example of doctor output. The prose two sections above it already tells the agent to report the number the tool returns rather than this one, but the example is still a stated count and it is still read as one.

The 'What you get' table in the release section. It stated 57 while rules.json carried 59, and it was invisible because CHANGELOG.md was not in the sweep -- the same drift class the gate was built for, in the one file a customer reads first.

known_gaps: A THIRD prose site lives in the generator's own repository, which is private, so no check here can reach it. It is the one copy of the count that is still unguarded.

Two code sites assert a lower bound rather than a count: .github/workflows/checks.yml ('at least 20') and plugins/zebra-bi/mcp/test-real-project.js ('the catalogue is down to N'). A floor does not go stale, so they are deliberately out of scope for this gate.
